For \(\alpha=(j,\omega)\in\Omega\), use the predicate \(\mathsf{Succ}_{\alpha}\) from Definition~\(\mathrm{Switching\ cover\ incidence}\).  It is important that positivity occurs in this predicate only for the event that is actually conditioned upon.  A zero-probability cell that is never used neither appears in a denominator nor enters the argument.

Suppose the full correctly typed run on \(\mathcal R(E_0)\) returns nonfailure.  By Definition~\(\mathrm{Structural\ target\mbox{-}factor\ tuple}\), its outer factorization has factors \(C_1,\ldots,C_k\); by the definition of \(\Omega\), its concrete loop contains every \(\alpha=(j,\omega)\).  The complete source search for a fixed branch ranges over every decoded source triple.  Nonfailure therefore implies
\[
 \forall\alpha\in\Omega\quad
 \exists(S_{\alpha},\ell_{\alpha},T_{\alpha},\tau_{\alpha})
 \text{ represented in }E_0:
 \mathsf{Succ}_{\alpha}(S_{\alpha},\ell_{\alpha},T_{\alpha},\tau_{\alpha})=1.
 \tag{1}
\]
This is a direct property of the operational run.  It does not invoke a semantic completeness theorem.

All sets in (1) are finite.  Choose the lexicographically first witness for each \(\alpha\).  Success and Proposition~\(\mathrm{Connected\mbox{-}ancestor\ obstruction}\) imply
\[
 \mathfrak O(T_{\alpha},C_j)=\varnothing,
 \tag{2}
\]
because a nonempty obstruction is equivalent to failure of that factor call.  Lemma~\(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) then permits the canonical finite transcript with at most \(|T_{\alpha}|\) strict restrictions.

Create one sparse record for each \(\alpha\), with the \(q_M\)-bit canonical index of \(\alpha\), the selected protocol, label, and source, and the canonical transcript.  Sorting these records gives exactly \(M\) nonempty records, and each positive index occurs once.  Every local legality, support, ancestry, and transcript check follows from (1); in particular, only the \(M\) selected events require positive probability.  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{Prot}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\subseteq\operatorname{Prot}(E_0).
 \tag{3}
\]
Since \(c(a)\geq0\) by Assumption~\(\mathrm{Binary\ rational\ cost}\), Definition~\(\mathrm{Distinct\mbox{-}protocol\ cost}\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})
 &=\sum_{S\in\operatorname{Prot}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})}\sum_{a\in S}c(a)\\
 &\leq\sum_{S\in\operatorname{Prot}(E_0)}\sum_{a\in S}c(a)
 =\operatorname{Cost}(E_0).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{4}
\]
For every branch, its selected record contributes a successful source to \(\mathcal R(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\).  Thus the exhaustive complete run on that collection returns nonfailure.  All parser and local checks also hold, so Definition~\(\mathrm{Sparse\ switching\ operational\ acceptance}\) yields
\[
 \operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}(Q,E_{\mathrm{sw}};G)=1.
 \tag{5}
\]

Conversely, if (5) holds, the acceptance definition itself constructs \(\mathcal R(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\), executes the complete run, and requires a nonfailure result.  It also requires every branch index exactly once.  Hence the records witness precisely \(\forall\alpha\exists(S,\ell,T,\tau)\), with no exchange of quantifiers.  Both directions concern operational return values only, completing the proof.

Let an operationally accepting witness presentation be given.  If one protocol--slice--source triple is reused for several branches, copy its fixed fields once for each of those branch indices and attach the corresponding concrete transcript.  Distinct-protocol charging makes this splitting cost neutral.  Delete every index-zero marker; it supplies no successful branch, acceptance is unchanged, and cost cannot increase because all action costs are nonnegative.  Since the positive indices partition \(\{1,\ldots,M\}\), the result has exactly \(M\) nonempty records and at most \(M\) distinct protocols.

For each record, Proposition~\(\mathrm{Connected\mbox{-}ancestor\ obstruction}\) makes success equivalent to absence of an obstruction, and Lemma~\(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) gives at most \(n\) strict restrictions.  We now exhibit the promised finite encoding rather than hiding its framing.  Encode the number of transcript rows first and then pad to \(n+1\) rows.  A row has a presence bit and the three \(n\)-bit masks \((U_r,H_r,B_r)\); all reachability, connectivity, and literal comparisons are recomputed from \(G\), the branch index, and the source label.  With
\[
 q=\left\lceil\log_2(n+L+M+2)\right\rceil\geq1,
\]
the row-count code, the presence bits, the masks, and the constant end markers use at most
\[
 8(n+1)^2q=b_{\tau}
 \tag{6}
\]
bits.  Thus this is a concrete realization of the bound in Lemma~\(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\).

The normalized list has \(r=M\).  By Definition~\(\mathrm{Sparse\ switching\ acquisition\ certificate}\), its Elias-gamma record-count prefix has exactly
\[
 2\lfloor\log_2(M+1)\rfloor+1
 \tag{7}
\]
bits.  Every record has \(m+L+q_M+n(1+L)\) fixed bits and at most \(b_{\tau}\) transcript bits.  Equations (6)--(7) give
\[
 N_{\mathrm{sw}}
 \leq2\lfloor\log_2(M+1)\rfloor+1
 +M\bigl(m+L+q_M+n(1+L)+b_{\tau}\bigr)
 =B_{\mathrm{sw}}.
 \tag{8}
\]
In particular, the ownership term is \(Mq_M\), not \(M^2\).

If a generic collection \(E_0\) makes the complete operational run return nonfailure, Theorem~\(\mathrm{Sparse\ switching\ source\ normal\ form}\) supplies a switching witness of cost at most \(\operatorname{Cost}(E_0)\); the preceding normalization preserves that domination.  The universe of protocol masks, literal masks, labelled source masks, branch indices, and canonical transcripts is finite.  Hence the set of normalized accepted strings satisfying (8) is finite.  When feasibility holds it is nonempty, so its finite set of exact binary-rational costs has a minimum; lexicographic order chooses a unique first minimizer \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}\).  It obeys (8) and dominates every accepting generic acquisition.  The proof never places any oracle reply inside the certificate, so those reply bits remain charged only to \(N_{\mathcal O}\).

Operational feasibility and Lemma~\(\mathrm{Sparse\ canonical\ certificate\ bound}\) give a nonempty finite set of canonical accepted certificates of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{sw}}\); exact binary-rational costs attain their minimum there.  Its lexicographically first minimizer is \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}\), and the same lemma gives
\[
 N_{E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}}\leq B_{\mathrm{sw}}.
 \tag{18}
\]

Theorem~\(\mathrm{Switching\ weighted\mbox{-}cover\ frontier}\) constructs the complete relation \(K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\) with at most \(2^{|\mathcal A|}\) oracle queries and proves that its minimum-weight cover value equals \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}\).  Its branch-mask recurrence or protocol-subset enumeration therefore computes the exact value in
\[
 2^{O(|\mathcal A|+|\mathrm{LIT}|+\min\{M,2^{|\mathcal A|}\})}
 \operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})
 \tag{19}
\]
time.  All rational sums are compared exactly because their summands are binary rationals.

To recover the stipulated lexicographically first certificate without enumerating all strings of length \(B_{\mathrm{sw}}\), retain during incidence construction the finite ordered list of successful witnesses for every pair \((S,\alpha)\).  Given a proposed encoding prefix, delete witness records incompatible with that prefix and force every record already fixed by it.  The cover recurrence (or the protocol-subset enumerator) then decides whether an accepted completion of total cost \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}\) exists: the uncovered universe is the set of unforced branch indices, and a protocol covers exactly those remaining branches for which a compatible successful witness remains.  Trying the next bit in increasing order preserves the invariant that the current prefix has an optimum completion.  At the first complete string the result is optimal; if a lexicographically smaller optimum existed, its first differing bit would have passed the same completion test.  This self-reduction performs a polynomial number of exact-cover calls in the explicit incidence and output length.  By \(M\leq k2^{|\mathrm{LIT}|}\) and (18), that polynomial factor is absorbed in (19).

Decoding the resulting sparse records outputs the protocol and literal masks, labelled source masks, \(q_M\)-bit singleton indices, and canonical transcripts.  The incidence construction caches the reply for each protocol mask, so every issued query and every read support or handle bit is counted once in \(N_{\mathcal O}\).  The greedy conclusion and its faster running time are exactly (17) and (14) of the weighted-cover theorem.  Finally, both the optimization identity and the verifier are stated solely in terms of \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}\); no semantic completeness, scalar functional evaluation, or positivity of an unused cell has entered the proof.

Let
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\{E_{\mathrm{sw}}:\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}(Q,E_{\mathrm{sw}};G)=1\}.
\]
If this set is nonempty, Theorem~\(\mathrm{Cost\mbox{-}optimal\ sparse\ certificate}\) returns \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}\) and
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star})<+\infty.
 \tag{20}
\]
If it is empty, the convention in Definition~\(\mathrm{Switching\ optimal\ acquisition\ cost}\) gives \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}=+\infty\).  These cases are disjoint and exhaustive.

The weighted-cover identity gives
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \bigcup_{S\in\Pi}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega.
 \tag{21}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{Sparse\ canonical\ certificate\ bound}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists E_{\mathrm{sw}}\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}
 \text{ with }N_{\mathrm{sw}}\leq B_{\mathrm{sw}},
 \tag{22}
\]
and Theorem~\(\mathrm{Sparse\ switching\ source\ normal\ form}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists E_0\text{ finite and correctly typed such that the complete run on }
 \mathcal R(E_0)\text{ returns nonfailure}.
 \tag{23}
\]
Negating (21)--(23) proves all infeasibility equivalences.

Constructing the incidence and running the faster of the two exact cover algorithms has the query and time bounds in (19).  It decides whether the union in (21) is all of \(\Omega\), so it decides the alternative.  In the negative case there is no output certificate to encode.  Because (21)--(23) compare operational predicates only, their negations do not assert semantic nonidentifiability.

Fix \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}\in\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}\).  For \(B\subseteq V\), Definition~\(\mathrm{Ordinary\ full\mbox{-}kernel\ design\ embedding}\) gives
\[
 S_B=\{s\}\cup\{r_v:v\in B\}\cup\{\rho_v:v\in V\}.
 \tag{25}
\]
It has one fresh-unit SELECT, executes every mechanism at most once, respects precedence, has no conflicting pair, and satisfies the stipulated ordinary CTF-REALIZE condition.  Thus \(S_B\in\Pi\).  Independence and uniformity of the RAND coordinates imply, for every \(b\in\mathfrak X_B\),
\[
 \Pr\{R_B=b\}=\prod_{v\in B}|\mathfrak X_v|^{-1}>0.
 \tag{26}
\]
The slice and label definitions then give
\[
 \operatorname{Slice}(S_B,\ell_{B,b})
 =P_b(V\setminus B)=Q[V\setminus B](\cdot;b).
 \tag{27}
\]
All vertices are READ, so measured ancestry holds.

Let \(\mathbf B\) be ordinary full-kernel identifying.  Its target contains every \((x,s)\), and its source family contains every \((B,b)\) in (27).  Lemma~\(\mathrm{Single\mbox{-}world\ operational\ specialization}\) makes the complete translated run return nonfailure for every target cell.  Applying Theorem~\(\mathrm{Sparse\ switching\ source\ normal\ form}\) separately to each cell produces \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{x,s}\).  Use the shared protocol set \(\mathcal P_{\mathbf B}=\{S_B:B\in\{B_i\}_{\mathrm{distinct}}\}\), as required by the batch definition.  By (26), every actually used label event is positive.  The zero SELECT and READ costs and (25) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P_{\mathbf B}}\sum_{a\in S}c(a)
 &=\sum_{B\in\{B_i\}_{\mathrm{distinct}}}\sum_{v\in B}c(r_v)\\
 &=\sum_{B\in\{B_i\}_{\mathrm{distinct}}}\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{28}
\]
Hence the forward batch is accepted and has exactly the ordinary shared acquisition cost.

Conversely, let \(E_{\mathrm{batch}}=(\mathcal P,(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{x,s})_{x,s})\) be accepted in the embedded catalogue.  For \(S\in\mathcal P\), put \(B(S)=\{v:r_v\in S\}\).  Adding every missing zero-cost READ preserves SELECT cardinality, mechanism use, precedence, conflicts, physical compatibility, and cost.  Coalesce protocols with the same \(B(S)\) and call the resulting ordinary collection \(\mathbf B(E_{\mathrm{batch}})\).

It remains to show that every source slice used by a component certificate is available from the corresponding full ordinary family.  Suppose its label fixes RAND coordinates \(D\subseteq B(S)\) at \(b_D\), leaves the remaining RAND coordinates unconditioned, and conditions on a READ event \(R=r\).  For every recorded event \(A\), independence and uniformity give
\[
 \Pr_S(A\mid R_D=b_D,R=r)
 =\frac{
 \displaystyle\sum_{b_{B(S)\setminus D}}
 \left(\prod_{v\in B(S)\setminus D}|\mathfrak X_v|^{-1}\right)
 P_{(b_D,b_{B(S)\setminus D})}(A,R=r)}{
 \displaystyle\sum_{b_{B(S)\setminus D}}
 \left(\prod_{v\in B(S)\setminus D}|\mathfrak X_v|^{-1}\right)
 P_{(b_D,b_{B(S)\setminus D})}(R=r)}.
 \tag{29}
\]
The denominator is positive because this conditioning event is actually used by an accepted record.  Formula (29) is a finite rational operation on members of \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B(E_{\mathrm{batch}})}\).  It invokes no positivity for an unasserted READ cell.  Therefore every used source and marginal factor is in the permitted deterministic preprocessing closure of that ordinary family.  Applying the single-world specialization lemma to each accepted component proves ordinary operational acceptance for every cell \((x,s)\), so \(\mathbf B(E_{\mathrm{batch}})\) is full-kernel identifying.

Coalescing and the zero SELECT and READ costs give
\[
 \sum_{B\in\mathbf B(E_{\mathrm{batch}})}\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v
 \leq\sum_{S\in\mathcal P}\sum_{a\in S}c(a).
 \tag{30}
\]
Taking infima in (28) gives \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{batch}}\leq\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{ord}}\), and taking infima in (30) gives the reverse inequality.  The same maps prove equality of feasibility, hence
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{batch}}=\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{ord}}.
 \tag{31}
\]

The cited Akbari--Etesami--Kiyavash theorem gives a polynomial reduction from minimum-weight hitting set to their ordinary minimum-cost full-kernel intervention problem, and their cited corollary gives the \((1-o(1))\ln|V|\) threshold under the stated quasi-polynomial-time assumption.  Their displayed construction uses prohibitive auxiliary costs.  On a finite rational weighted instance with total original weight \(W\) and \(N\) vertices in the constructed graph, replace each prohibitive cost by the integer
\[
 C_{\mathrm{aux}}=(N+1)(W+1).
 \tag{32}
\]
An original hitting set has cost at most \(W\), so an exact optimum never selects an auxiliary vertex.  Any approximation with ratio below \(\ln N\leq N\) also has output cost less than \(NW<C_{\mathrm{aux}}\) and therefore cannot select one.  The binary encoding length of (32) is polynomial in the weighted input length.  Binary observed domains may be assigned because the reduction's identification obstructions are graphical.  Thus the cited hardness statements persist on the finite-rational, finite-discrete ordinary class.

Finally, (28)--(31) are cost-preserving reductions between that class and the batch SELECT--RAND--READ image.  The structural catalogue is polynomially written, but its complete law and support replies can be exponential and are supplied by \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\).  Consequently the transfer is relative to that oracle convention, with all returned bits charged to \(N_{\mathcal O}\); it is not a standard explicit-input NP-hardness assertion.  Because the construction concerns a finite batch and only SELECT--RAND--READ actions, it gives neither a batch-to-scalar reduction nor an approximation result for the general physical catalogue.

added_lemmas.statement:
For the switching incidence sets and protocol weights,
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\min_{\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:\,\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega}
   \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S),
\]
with value \(+\infty\) when no cover exists.  Writing \(m=|\mathcal A|\), \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\), and \(M=|\Omega|\), the complete incidence relation is constructible with at most \(2^m\) distinct source-oracle queries and \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) work, because \(M\leq k2^L\).  Branch-mask dynamic programming or protocol-subset enumeration then computes the exact optimum in
\[
 2^{O(m+L+\min\{M,2^m\})}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})
\]
time.  Weighted greedy on this explicit protocol-to-branch incidence returns an accepted certificate of cost at most \(H_M\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}\), where \(H_M=\sum_{r=1}^{M}r^{-1}\), in \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) time whenever the instance is feasible.  This is a protocol-cover guarantee after incidence enumeration, not a polynomial-time action-cover guarantee.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal P(E)\) be the distinct protocols occurring in the nonempty records of an accepted sparse certificate.  Each branch \(\alpha\) occurs in exactly one such record, and that record passes the predicate \(\mathsf{Succ}_{\alpha}\).  Hence
\[
 \Omega\subseteq\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P(E)}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S).
 \tag{9}
\]
The reverse inclusion is automatic because each incidence set is a subset of \(\Omega\), so \(\mathcal P(E)\) is a cover.  Removing index-zero markers can only lower cost, and therefore
\[
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P(E)}w(S)\leq\operatorname{Cost}(E).
 \tag{10}
\]

Conversely, let \(\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi\) cover \(\Omega\).  For every branch \(\alpha\), choose the first \(S\in\mathcal P\) with \(\alpha\in K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\), and then choose the first witness \((\ell,T,\tau)\) in the existential definition of that incidence.  Make one singleton-index record for \(\alpha\).  Every local check holds by \(\mathsf{Succ}_{\alpha}=1\), and every branch is represented exactly once.  Each branch has a successful source in the decoded complete collection, so the full operational run returns nonfailure and \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}=1\).  Omitting protocols of \(\mathcal P\) unused by these records can only lower the nonnegative cost.  Taking minima in the two directions (9)--(10) proves
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\min_{\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:\,\cup_{S\in\mathcal P}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega}
   \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S).
 \tag{11}
\]
This equality is derived from operational acceptance and distinct-protocol charging; it is not a definition of the causal query.

We next construct every incidence bit.  Enumerate the \(2^m\) protocol masks.  Catalogue scans check SELECT cardinality, mechanism use, precedence, and conflicts, while the published CTF-REALIZE runtime lemma checks physical compatibility in polynomial time.  Query each legal mask at most once and cache its immutable reply.  For a non-\(\bot\) reply enumerate the \(2^L\) literal masks, reject inconsistent labels, and use the returned support table to test the event actually conditioned upon.  From each surviving slice, the canonical ancestral and district decomposition lists at most \(n\) single-district factors.  Measured ancestry is a graph-and-action check.

For a factor \(C_j\), suppose its free request positions have domain sizes \(h_1,\ldots,h_r\).  The equality type is induced by the assignment and supplies no extra independent choice.  Since the literal table contains one request literal for each possible value,
\[
 |\Omega_j|=\prod_{u=1}^{r}h_u
 \leq2^{\sum_{u=1}^{r}h_u}
 \leq2^L,
 \qquad
 M=\sum_{j=1}^{k}|\Omega_j|\leq k2^L.
 \tag{12}
\]
For every enumerated \(\alpha,S,\ell,T\), instantiate the value matches and run the ancestor--district recursion.  Proposition~\(\mathrm{Connected\mbox{-}ancestor\ obstruction}\) decides failure, and Lemma~\(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) supplies the canonical transcript on success.  Therefore all and only the true incidence bits are recorded.  The number of branch checks is at most
\[
 2^m2^L nM
 \leq 2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}).
 \tag{13}
\]
Reading the exact support replies contributes their actual total length \(N_{\mathcal O}\).  Thus (13), including graph work and exact cost arithmetic, is
\[
 2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O}),
 \tag{14}
\]
and uses no more than \(2^m\) distinct oracle queries.  Notice that zero-mass unused cells are merely table entries; no division by them occurs.

List the protocols with nonempty incidence as \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\), where \(p\leq2^m\).  For \(U\subseteq\Omega\), initialize \(D_0(\varnothing)=0\), \(D_0(U)=+\infty\) for \(U\ne\varnothing\), and set
\[
 D_i(U)=\min\{D_{i-1}(U),D_{i-1}(U\setminus K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S_i))+w(S_i)\}.
 \tag{15}
\]
Induction on \(i\) shows that \(D_i(U)\) is the least weight of a subcollection of the first \(i\) protocols covering \(U\): an optimum either omits \(S_i\), or includes it and leaves \(U\setminus K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S_i)\).  Thus (15) evaluates (11) in \(O(p2^M)\) arithmetic operations.  Alternatively, enumerate the \(2^p\) protocol subsets and test their unions.  Choosing the faster alternative and adding (14) gives
\[
 2^{O(m+L+\min\{M,2^m\})}
 \operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O}).
 \tag{16}
\]

Finally consider the weighted greedy algorithm recorded in the published weighted-greedy lemma.  We derive the exact constant needed here.  First take every zero-cost protocol that covers a new branch.  Thereafter, when \(r\) branches remain, an optimum cover of cost \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}\) covers those branches, so summing newly covered branch counts over its protocols is at least \(r\).  Hence some optimum protocol has ratio at most \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}/r\) between its cost and its number of newly covered branches.  Greedy chooses no larger a ratio.  Charge that ratio to each branch newly covered in the step.  As \(r\) decreases from \(M\) to \(1\), the total charge, which equals greedy cost, is at most
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}\sum_{r=1}^{M}\frac1r
 =H_M\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}.
 \tag{17}
\]
If the optimum is zero, the initial zero-cost phase covers every branch and (17) still holds.  The cover-to-certificate construction above yields an accepted sparse certificate.  Greedy is polynomial in the explicit incidence size, so (14) is its total construction time.  This proves every assertion.
added_lemmas.justification: The protocol-to-branch incidence exposes the exact finite weighted-cover object induced by operational switching acceptance.
added_lemmas.gap: The earlier certificate-string search hid the shared-protocol combinatorics and incurred an avoidable exponential dependence on the certificate encoding length.
added_lemmas.consumer: The exact optimizer uses the faster of branch-mask dynamic programming and protocol-subset enumeration, while weighted greedy supplies an explicit protocol-cover benchmark.

added_lemmas.statement: On the ordinary SELECT--RAND--READ image, for every cell \(Q_{x,s}\) and complete ordinary source family \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B}\), the complete ordinary single-world procedure accepts \(Q[S_0]\) at \((x,s)\) if and only if the complete translated unconditional \(\operatorname{CTFIDU}^{+}\) run returns nonfailure for \(Q_{x,s}\).  The equivalence remains valid after deterministic formation of a marginal or a conditional from a supplied full kernel when, and only when, the denominator of that actually used conditional is positive.  It imposes no positivity on unused cells and makes no claim for cross-world or nonordinary inputs.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a target cell \((x,s)\).  Its translated event contains only variables from the single intervention world \(x\).  Counterfactual ancestor expansion therefore deletes the variables fixed by \(x\) and retains exactly the ordinary ancestors of \(S_0\); the induced bidirected districts are the ordinary c-components on the same vertex sets.  The translated source indexed by \((B,b)\) is, by definition, the full ordinary kernel \(P_b(V\setminus B)\).

We compare the two recursions by induction on the current source-factor vertex set \(U\).  In the base case the target set equals \(U\), and both procedures return the same marginal of the same full kernel.  Otherwise the value-matching closure in the translated call removes exactly those variables fixed by the ordinary intervention labels.  The published \(\operatorname{IDENTIFY}^{+}\) recursion therefore has the same ancestor set and the same district containing the target as the ordinary fixing recursion.  If the closure is all of \(U\) and is larger than the target, both return failure; if it is proper, both recurse on the same strictly smaller district.  The strict decrease in the published recursion makes the induction terminate.  Thus their return statuses agree for the cell.

A marginal is a finite sum of cells of the supplied kernel.  If a used source is conditioned on an event \(R=r\), then
\[
 P_b(A\mid R=r)=\frac{P_b(A,R=r)}{P_b(R=r)}
 \tag{24}
\]
is defined exactly when the displayed denominator is positive.  Replacing the used conditional by (24) before either recursion leaves every subsequent symbolic equality unchanged.  No denominator is introduced for any other cell.  Hence the induction also covers the permitted preprocessing, proving the stated event-local and operational equivalence.
added_lemmas.justification: The batch boundary needs a typed cellwise correspondence between ordinary single-world recursion and the translated operational procedure.
added_lemmas.gap: A finite all-cells kernel cannot be treated as one scalar counterfactual query.
added_lemmas.consumer: The ordinary embedding applies the sparse normal form separately to every cell while sharing protocol charges across the batch.

added_lemmas.statement: The minimum-weight hitting-set problem reduces in polynomial time to the ordinary minimum-cost intervention problem.  In the cited construction, original vertices retain their hitting-set weights, auxiliary vertices have prohibitive infinite cost, and finite-cost identifying interventions are exactly the hitting sets with the same cost.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Suppose a finite acquired collection \(E_0\) makes the correctly typed full unconditional procedure \(\operatorname{CTFIDU}^{+}(G,Q,\mathcal R(E_0))\) operationally return a nonfailure result.  Then there is a canonical sparse switching certificate \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}\), using only protocol--slice--source triples represented in \(E_0\), with exactly one nonempty record for each \(\alpha\in\Omega\), at most \(M\) distinct protocols,
\[
 \operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}(Q,E_{\mathrm{sw}};G)=1,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\leq\operatorname{Cost}(E_0).
\]
Each record names its singleton branch by a \(q_M\)-bit index and supplies one positive, measured-ancestry source triple and a finite successful transcript.  Conversely, acceptance by \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}\) implies that the complete run on \(\mathcal R(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\) returns nonfailure.  This is only an equivalence of the two operational acceptance events; it neither exchanges \(\forall\alpha\exists\) with \(\exists\forall\) nor supplies a semantic completeness extension under event-local positivity.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The old claim was tied to grouped ownership masks and could be read as invoking semantic CTFIDU+ completeness under an event-local positivity class not established by the frozen cited result.  The repaired claim uses singleton indices and narrows the conclusion to exact operational acceptance equivalence.

\[
 b_{\tau}=8(n+1)^2\left\lceil\log_2(n+L+M+2)\right\rceil.
\]

The result has exactly \(M\) records, at most \(M\) protocols, and exact length at most
